Q: HandbrakeCLI can't find files when run from Python A:

Your issue is caused by how you're passing the -i and -o arguments to subprocess.run().

Right now you're doing this:

f"-i {path}/{file}",
f"-o {path}/{make_new_name(file)}"

This passes -i /path/to/file.mkv as one single argument, but HandBrakeCLI expects:

hb_stream_open: open  /path/to/my/videos/S00E00.mkv failed
scan: unrecognized file type

Notice the extra space before /path/....

Check this your old and Updated code, I hope is will help you.

Q: Observability for a GitHub Copilot custom agent (Visual Studio Code) A:

The core problem you're describing - observability for AI agent interactions without relying on platform-specific hacks, is exactly what OpenTelemetry-based solutions are designed for.

Rather than scraping VS Code's internal files, you can intercept at the LLM API layer. If your custom agent makes calls to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, you can route those through a reverse proxy that records every request and response with full context.

AIR Blackbox does this. It's an open-source observability layer for AI agents. The setup is one line:

python

# Point your agent's base_url at the gateway
client = OpenAI(base_url="http://localhost:8080/v1")

Every LLM call gets traced via OpenTelemetry, grouped into replayable episodes, and stored locally — no cloud dependency. You get:

  • Full request/response logging for every LLM call

  • PII redaction before traces hit your backend

  • Traces viewable in Jaeger (localhost:16686)

For your specific use case with a Copilot custom agent that ships with an MCP server, the MCP Policy Gateway can also add observability at the MCP tool layer, covering the tool calls your agent makes.

This approach is platform-agnostic works across VS Code, CLI, PyCharm, or any client -- because it operates at the network layer rather than depending on IDE internals.

Q: bootstrap modal: Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'backdrop') modal.js:158 A:

In my case I got this error since I was passing data-bs-target attribute and left the # from the target string.

So basically any incorrect reference to the ID of the modal will result in this error.

Q: Consume a REST API in codeigniter controller A:

Add below to your curl options

curl_setopt($curl, CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER, array(
  'APIKEY: admin@123',
  'Content-Type: application/json',
   ));

also update

$config['rest_key_name'] = 'APIKEY';

in rest.php file inside config folder of your codeigniter settings. By default it is 'X-API-KEY'

This may help to somebody else looking for a solution, if OP has resolved it himself/herself.
